lines.japanese: というわけで、メンマの屋台という選択肢のなくなった今、俺は迷わずパルクレープへやって来た──
lines.english: So, with Menma's ramen cart no longer an option, I came straight to Paru Crêpes—

lines.japanese: ──のだが。
lines.english: —only to find...

lines.japanese: 「おう、ドラ」
lines.english: “Yo, Dora.”

lines.japanese: 「うす」
lines.english: “'Sup.”

lines.japanese: パル姐さんの呼びかけに答えるのが一瞬遅れたのは、店の脇の奇妙な一団に注意を奪われてしまったからだ。
lines.english: I was a second late answering Paru. The odd little group beside the shop had stolen my attention.

lines.japanese: 老若男女バラバラの五人組が、クレープと『柳木原ワクワク食べあるきＭＡＰ』を手に議論している。
lines.english: Five people of all different ages were standing there with crepes and copies of the *Yanagihara Fun-Filled Food Crawl Map*, deep in discussion.

lines.japanese: ひとりは皺だらけな作業着のジイさん。
lines.english: One was an old man in wrinkled work clothes.

lines.japanese: ひとりはパリッとしたエリートサラリーマン風。
lines.english: One looked like an elite salaryman in a crisp suit.

lines.japanese: またひとりは冗談みたいな厚化粧の、でっぷりしたオバはん。
lines.english: Another was a portly middle-aged woman wearing a comical amount of makeup.

lines.japanese: そして──
lines.english: And—

lines.japanese: ──残り二名は知った顔だった。
lines.english: —the last two were faces I knew.

lines.japanese: 「なにアレ」
lines.english: “What the hell is that?”

lines.japanese: つうか、アイツら。
lines.english: I mean, those people.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、メンマんとこの新しい常連さァ。あんたらが卒業してったあとの、ニュージェネレーションってやつさね」
lines.english: “Oh, Menma's new regulars. The new generation that came along after you kids graduated.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: べつに卒業した覚えはないけど、以前より足が遠のいてたことは確かだ。よもやそのあいだに世代交代が起こっていたとは。
lines.english: I didn't remember graduating, but it was true I hadn't been around as often. Who knew there'd been a whole changing of the guard while I was gone?

lines.japanese: 「つってもメンマの野郎、こないだ屋台たたんじまいやがったろ？　だもんで、やっこさんが新しい店開くまで、どこを溜まり場にするかってェ相談をしてンだとさ」
lines.english: “Thing is, that jackass Menma went and closed his cart, remember? So they're hashing out where to hang around until he opens his new place.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん……」
輪の中心にいる小娘を眺めながら、俺はいつかメンマの言った言葉を思いだしていた。
lines.english: As I watched the girl at the center of the circle, I remembered something Menma had once said.

lines.japanese: “ドラたちは離れてく時期みてえだが、おまえはこれからなんだろ、新人”
lines.english: “Looks like Dora and his crowd are starting to move on, but you’re just getting started, aren’t you, rookie?”

lines.japanese: “だから次は、おまえの周りにひとが集まるのかもしれないぞ、鳴”
lines.english: “So maybe you’ll be the one people gather around next, Naru.”

lines.japanese: もしかしたら、やつの予言は現実になろうとしているのかもしれない。
lines.english: Maybe his prediction was about to come true.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうだドラ、あんた宛てに預かり物があったんだよ」
lines.english: “Oh, right, Dora. Somebody left something here for you.”

lines.japanese: ふとパルさんが小物入れを探りながら言った。
lines.english: Paru spoke as she rummaged through a little storage box.

lines.japanese: 「あ？　誰から」
lines.english: “Huh? Who?”

lines.japanese: 「エージ。ほいよ」
lines.english: “Eiji. Here.”
“Whoa.”

lines.japanese: 投げわたされたそれは、小さな鍵だった。
lines.english: What she tossed me was a small key.

lines.japanese: エージの鍵。
lines.english: Eiji's key.

lines.japanese: 鍵を預かるだけでゲーマンもらえる仕事。
lines.english: The job that paid fifty thousand yen just to hold on to a key.

lines.japanese: 今ごろになってエージからのメールを思いだす。そうだ、ブツの受け取り場所には、パルクレープを指定されていたんだ。
lines.english: Only now did I remember Eiji's email. Right. He'd named Paru Crêpes as the place where I was supposed to pick the thing up.

lines.japanese: 「何の鍵だか知らないけどね、おまえさん、あんまりエージのチンピラ仕事に首突っこむもんじゃありゃーせんよ？」
lines.english: “I don't know what that key opens, but you oughtn't go sticking your nose into Eiji's hoodlum business.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、突っこんでねーっつの。その話はきっぱり断ったんだって。だからパルさん、これ返す」
lines.english: “I'm not. I turned him down flat. So here, take this back.”

lines.japanese: 「冗談じゃないよ。こちとら半日預かるのだって嫌だったんだ、これ以上あたしを巻きこまないどくれ」
lines.english: “Like hell. I hated holding it for half a day. Don't drag me any deeper into this.”

lines.japanese: 「マジかよ。俺、無関係なのに」
lines.english: “Seriously? This has nothing to do with me.”

lines.japanese: 溜息といっしょに放りなげたくなる。
lines.english: It made me want to sigh and throw the damn thing away.

lines.japanese: 「苦情だったら直接本人に言いねえ。無関係ってんなら、こっちもおんなしさ」
lines.english: “Take your complaints to the man himself. If you've got nothing to do with it, neither do I.”

lines.japanese: 「へーへー」
lines.english: “Yeah, yeah.”

lines.japanese: 俺はエージに電話をかけた。言うことはひとつ。鍵捨てるぞ。
lines.english: I called Eiji. I had one thing to tell him: I was throwing away his key.

lines.japanese: しかし返ってきたのはノーテンキなやつの声ではなく、事務的なアナウンスだった。
lines.english: Instead of his carefree voice, I got a businesslike recording.

lines.japanese: オ掛ケニナッタ電話ハ、電波ノ届カナイ所ニアルカ、電源ガ入ッテイナイ為オ繋ギ出来マセン。
lines.english: The number you have dialed is either outside the service area or the phone is switched off and cannot be reached.

lines.japanese: 「出ないのかい？」
lines.english: “Not answering?”

lines.japanese: 「くそっ、シカトぶっこいてる」
lines.english: “Shit. He’s ignoring me.”

lines.japanese: そういやあいつ、この電話じきに繋がらなくなるとか言ってたか……？
lines.english: Come to think of it, hadn't he said this number would stop working soon... ?

lines.japanese: うわ、めんどくせえ。怪しい臭いしかしてこねえ。
lines.english: Ugh, what a pain in the ass. This whole thing reeked of trouble.

lines.japanese: 「パルさん、コレ捨ててもいい」
lines.english: “Paru, can I throw this away?”

lines.japanese: 「いいんじゃない、あんたが責任取れんなら」
lines.english: “Sure, if you're prepared to take responsibility for it.”

lines.japanese: しかしその鍵に「人生がかかっている」とまで言いきったエージの言葉を思いだすと、煙草の吸いがらみたいにポイ捨てするのも気がひける。
lines.english: But then I remembered Eiji insisting that his life depended on this key. That made it hard to toss aside like a cigarette butt.

lines.japanese: 単なる冗談まがいのハッタリかもしれない。
lines.english: It could've been nothing but a half-joking bluff.

lines.japanese: しかし事実やつは、末端と言えど、そういう言葉が冗談ばかりでは済まされない世界に片足を突っこんでいる。
lines.english: But the fact remained that Eiji had one foot, low-ranking though it might be, in a world where words like that couldn't always be dismissed as jokes.

lines.japanese: どうするか、この鍵──
lines.english: What was I supposed to do with this key—

lines.japanese: ──悩んでいたら鳴と目が合った。
lines.english: —and while I was wondering, I made eye contact with Naru.

lines.japanese: 「あー、こんばんはードラさん」
lines.english: “Oh, good evening, Dora.”

lines.japanese: 場の作法にならって、やつは俺をあだ名で呼んだ。
lines.english: Following the local custom, she called me by my nickname.

lines.japanese: 「おう」
lines.english: “Yo.”

lines.japanese: こいつにそう呼ばれるのは、ずいぶん懐かしい気がした。
lines.english: It felt like ages since she'd called me that.

lines.japanese: 「ちょりーっす、ドラっ先輩！」
lines.english: “Yooo, Dora! My man!”

lines.japanese: おまえはその名で呼ぶな。部外者だろ。
lines.english: You don't get to call me that. You're an outsider.

lines.japanese: いや──
lines.english: No—

lines.japanese: ──違うか、いまでは俺の方が部外者だな。
lines.english: —that wasn't right. These days, I was the outsider.

lines.japanese: ドラキュラのドラがやって来ても、残りの連中はまったく興味を示さない。
lines.english: Even with Dora the vampire standing right there, none of the others showed the slightest interest.

lines.japanese: 「いよいよ俺の時代も終わりか……こういう風にして世界は変わってくンだな……」
lines.english: “So my era finally ends... This is how the world changes, huh...”

lines.japanese: 「ハ？　なに言ってんすか先輩」
lines.english: “Huh? What're you talking about, man?”

lines.japanese: 「だいじょぶですよう、私たちが遊んであげますからー」
lines.english: “Don't worry. We'll play with you.”

lines.japanese: 「へーへー」
lines.english: “Yeah, yeah.”

lines.japanese: 俺は例の鍵をポケットへ押しこむと、ミニバンに背を預けて呆れた無気力を装った。
lines.english: I shoved the key into my pocket, leaned against the minivan, and put on a show of world-weary indifference.

lines.japanese: 仲間をふたりも持っていかれたニュージェネレーションズの目には、俺がどんな風に映っているんだろう。ちょっとした優越感。
lines.english: How did I look to the New Generation, now that I'd stolen two of their companions away? The thought gave me a small, smug thrill.

lines.japanese: 「つかおまえ、いまメンマんとこの常連なんだって？」
lines.english: “So you're a regular at Menma's now?”

lines.japanese: いつも鳳たちとツルんでいる、ハニィＰだかＱだかいうギャル男に訊いてみた。
lines.english: I asked the flashy guy who was always hanging around with the Ohtoris—Honey P, or Q, or whatever his name was.

lines.japanese: 「そおなんスよ。いや、ちょっと前？　花水木通りブラブラ歩いてたら、アレ？　皇帝の妹がラーメン食ってんじゃん、つって」
lines.english: “Yeah, man. Or, like, a while back? I was cruising down Flowering Dogwood Street and I go, huh? Ain't that the Emperor's little sister eating ramen?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、食べてましたー」
lines.english: “I was eating ramen.”

lines.japanese: 「ほんで、声かけんべーつって近付いてったら、その隣りに俺の好み直撃っつーか？　どストライクのねーさんいたもんで。うーわマジパネえわッつって思わず俺──」
lines.english: “So I'm like, let's go say hey, and I head over, and sitting next to her is this older babe who's, like, dead center of my strike zone, y'know? I'm all, holy shit, she's smokin', and before I know it, I—”

lines.japanese: 「──あ、そういや隼人先輩も、パル姐とは知り合いらしッスね」
lines.english: “Oh, right. You know Paru too, don't you, Hayato?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　あァ、まァ」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh, yeah.”

lines.japanese: 知り合いなんて他人行儀な呼び方はしっくり来ないけど、トモダチってのもなんか違う。成田隼人と春日春江の関係を適切に定義する日本語を、俺は知らない。
lines.english: *Acquaintance* felt too distant, but *friend* didn’t feel quite right either. I didn’t know any word that properly defined the relationship between Hayato Narita and Harue Kasuga.

lines.japanese: 「っつーわけで、よろっす先輩！　俺メンマさんとこだけじゃなくて、この店の常連にもなりましたんで！」
lines.english: “Anyhoo, you’ll be seein’ me around, man! Menma’s ain’t the only place I’m a regular now. I’m a regular here too!”

lines.japanese: 「おまえクレープとか好きだったの」
lines.english: “You always liked crepes?”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃあ、だって、サイコーじゃないスかここの胸！」
lines.english: “I mean, c'mon. Have you seen the tits in this place?”

lines.japanese: 「胸かよ」
lines.english: “The tits?”

lines.japanese: 「ま、おもに胸なんスけど、そんでなくても、俺ああいう気風のいいオネエさん超タイプなんスよねえ！」
lines.english: “Okay, yeah, mostly the tits. But even without those, I'm way into feisty older chicks like her!”

lines.japanese: 「やめとけ、やめとけ。ありゃ、おまえみたいなチャラいのに落ちるタマじゃねえぞ」
lines.english: “Forget it. A woman like that isn't gonna fall for some flashy little player like you.”

lines.japanese: 「うーわ出た、出たよそういう下衆な発想。もー、あんたキレーな女と見たらすぐソレだ」
lines.english: “Wow, there it is. There it fucking is, that sleazy way of thinking. You see a hot chick and your mind goes straight there.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえにだけは言われたくねえよ」
lines.english: “I don't wanna hear that from you.”

lines.japanese: 「フッ……悪いですが成田さん、僕はもうとっくにそういう段階を卒業してるんです」
lines.english: “Hmph... Sorry, Narita, but I graduated from that phase a long time ago.”

lines.japanese: 「まー、パルさんには出会って１０秒でフラれちゃいましたからねー」
lines.english: “Well, Paru did reject him within ten seconds of meeting him.”

lines.japanese: 「うわああぁぁあーん！　笑えよ、無様な失恋男を笑えよ！」
lines.english: “Waaaaah! Go on, laugh! Laugh at the pathetic loser who got dumped!”

lines.japanese: いや、出会って１０秒で告白する度胸はある意味尊敬する。
lines.english: Honestly, working up the nerve to confess within ten seconds of meeting her was almost worthy of respect.

lines.japanese: 「まー、ピサロさんの場合、まず女性の胸を見て話す癖から直さないとー」
lines.english: “In Pizarro's case, he should probably start by breaking his habit of talking to a woman's chest.”

lines.japanese: 「つかピサロって誰」
lines.english: “Who the hell is Pizarro?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、俺俺」
lines.english: “Oh, me. Me.”

lines.japanese: ふーん。相変わらず続いてンのか、メンマ組の通り名文化。よそとは違う呼ばれ方をする、特別な聖域。
lines.english: Huh. So Menma's crowd still had its culture of street names. A special little sanctuary where people called you something different from everyone else.

lines.japanese: 「なるほどな。由来はなんとなく分かるわ、ピアスとか日サロとかその辺だろ」
lines.english: “I think I get it. Piercings, tanning salons, that kind of thing?”

lines.japanese: 「そそ。その辺もアリーので、なんだスペインの？　昔の航海者？　だか何だかにちなんでーつって、セクシーが付けてくれた仇名なんスよ」
lines.english: “Yeah, yeah, those too. Plus, uh, some Spanish guy? Old-time explorer? Something like that. Sexy came up with the name.”

lines.japanese: 「つかセクシーって誰」
lines.english: “And who the hell is Sexy?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、私私」
lines.english: “Oh, me. Me.”

lines.japanese: 「マジか。由来がさっぱり想像つかねえな」
lines.english: “Seriously? Can't imagine where that one came from.”

lines.japanese: 「見たまんまですよー」
lines.english: “Just look at me.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、実は俺らも、そこは謎なんスよ。本人がそう呼べ言うから、とりま呼んでるものの」
lines.english: “Actually, none of us get it either. She told us to call her that, so, y'know, we do.”

lines.japanese: 「あれー、皆さん近眼ですかー」
lines.english: “Oh my. Is everyone here nearsighted?”

lines.japanese: どうやら世代は変わっても、通り名の付け方が適当なのは変わらないみたいだ。ドラキュラのドラが言えた義理でもないが。
lines.english: Apparently, even if the generation changed, their method of handing out street names stayed just as arbitrary. Not that Dora the vampire had room to talk.

lines.japanese: 「他にはどんなのいんの」
lines.english: “What're the others called?”

lines.japanese: 離れて固まっている三人のニュージェネレーションズに目をやった。向こうは向こうで楽しそうだ。閉鎖的なのも相変わらずか。
lines.english: I looked toward the other three members of the New Generation, huddled off to one side. They seemed to be having plenty of fun among themselves. The cliquishness hadn't changed either.

lines.japanese: 「あのツナギ着てるジイちゃんが、ソージ」
lines.english: “That old dude in the coveralls is Souji.”

lines.japanese: チャラ男が指差す先に、清掃員風の作業着に身をつつんだ初老の男がいた。
lines.english: The flashy guy pointed at an older man dressed like a janitor.

lines.japanese: 「宗二？　通り名はないんだ」
lines.english: “Souji? So he doesn't have a street name?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、本名は源太郎で、仇名がソージ」
lines.english: “Nah, his real name's Gentarou. Souji's the nickname.”

lines.japanese: 「掃除屋さんということでー」
lines.english: “Souji means cleaning. He looks like a janitor.”

lines.japanese: 適当だな。本名セーイチだけど英字新聞柄のシャツを着てたからエージ、と同じぐらい適当だな。
lines.english: Arbitrary. About as arbitrary as calling Seiichi ‘Eiji’—English lettering—because he wore a shirt covered in English newspaper print.

lines.japanese: 「で、その隣りにいるスーツの兄さんが、ギルティ」
lines.english: “And the dude in the suit next to him is Guilty.”

lines.japanese: フレームの細い眼鏡とハイブランドの背広がハマってる、三十代ぐらいの男。セレブ然とした風貌は、大衆酒場や風俗店の乱立するこの辺りの景観からはおよそ浮いている。
lines.english: He looked to be in his thirties. The thin-framed glasses and designer suit suited him perfectly, but his high-society air stood out in a neighborhood packed with cheap bars and brothels.

lines.japanese: 「ギルティってどんな意味」
lines.english: “What does ‘guilty’ mean?”

lines.japanese: 俺は帰国子女のセクシーに訊いてみた。
lines.english: I asked Sexy, who had lived abroad.

lines.japanese: 「英語で有罪ですー」
lines.english: “It means you have been convicted of a crime.”

lines.japanese: 「え、あいつ前科とかあんの」
lines.english: “What, he's got a record?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、かつて衆議院議員への贈賄容疑で法廷には立たされたものの、なんやかんやあって最終的には無罪を勝ちとったそうですよー」
lines.english: “No. He was once brought to trial for allegedly bribing a member of the House of Representatives, but one thing led to another and he ultimately won an acquittal.”

lines.japanese: 「そ。だからノット・ギルティ。略してギルティ」
lines.english: “Right. So he's ‘not guilty.’ We shortened it to ‘Guilty.’”

lines.japanese: 「略したら意味真逆じゃねーか」
lines.english: “You shortened it into the exact opposite!”

lines.japanese: つか政治家への賄賂て。
lines.english: And hold on. Bribing a politician?

lines.japanese: いや、それは冤罪だったのか。にしても、そんなん疑われるような世界て。
lines.english: No, he had been falsely accused, apparently. Still, what sort of world did a man have to live in before anyone even suspected him of something like that?

lines.japanese: 「なんでそんなステージの高けー種族が、柳木原の屋台で庶民ラーメン食ってんだよ」
lines.english: “Why is somebody operating on that level eating working-class ramen at a cart in Yanagihara?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、私が紹介したんです。橋の上で思いつめた表情のまま、じっと川面を見下ろしていたもので。まーまー、にんにくラーメンでも啜って元気だしましょーよーと」
lines.english: “Oh, I introduced him. I saw him standing on a bridge, staring down at the river with this terribly troubled look, so I said, come now, let's have some garlic ramen and cheer you up.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああそう……それは、うん、いいことしたな……」
lines.english: “Oh. Uh, right... That was a good thing you did...”

lines.japanese: 思ったより重い話だったみたいだ。次へ行こう。
lines.english: That story was heavier than I'd expected. Moving on.

lines.japanese: 「あのオバちゃんは？」
lines.english: “What about the older lady?”

lines.japanese: 最後のひとりは、全体的にケバい巨漢の中年女だった。
lines.english: The last member was a huge, garishly made-up middle-aged woman.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、あのＬＲさん家のおかんみたいなひとは、現役」
lines.english: “Oh, the one who looks like LR's mom? She's Active Duty.”

lines.japanese: 「ゲンエキ？」
lines.english: “Active Duty?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、この仇名についちゃ説明すると長くなんスけどね。とりま時をさかのぼること二十年前、ピンフ通りの中ほどにこの世の楽園と謳われた一軒のソープがございまして、当時ここの一番人気だった泡姫──」
lines.english: “Well, that nickname takes a while to explain. Our tale begins twenty years ago, with a certain soapland halfway down Pinfu Street, reputed to be paradise on earth. At the time, its most popular soap girl—”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いい。もういい、由来分かった」
lines.english: “Nope, that's enough. I get it.”

lines.japanese: まあ、なんだ、いつまでも元気でがんばれ。俺は他人事だと思って、おばちゃんのふくよかな後ろ姿に目潰しピースを送った。
lines.english: Well, good for her. Keep going strong, lady. Secure in the knowledge that it was none of my business, I flashed an eye-gouging peace sign at the woman’s ample back.

lines.japanese: 「えー、わかんなーい。鳴さん何のことだか、さっぱりわかんなーい」
lines.english: “Oh, I don't understand. Naru has no idea what any of this means.”

lines.japanese: 「こっちはこっちで面倒くせーな……」
lines.english: “You're a pain in the ass in your own special way...”

lines.japanese: 「セクシーは名前のわりに清純系って設定らしいッス」
lines.english: “Apparently, Sexy's character concept is that she's actually the pure and innocent type.”

lines.japanese: 「いらねーだろ、その設定」
lines.english: “That character concept can go.”

lines.japanese: 「足跡ひとつない雪野原のように純潔ですよー」
lines.english: “I'm as pure as an untouched field of snow.”

lines.japanese: 「でもセクシーなんだろ」
lines.english: “But you're still Sexy?”

lines.japanese: 「うふん？　坊やはどっちのあたしがお好みかしら？」
lines.english: “Mmm? Which version of me does the little boy prefer?”

lines.japanese: 「どっちもきめえ」
lines.english: “Both are gross.”

lines.japanese: 「ぎゃふん」
lines.english: “Oof!”

lines.japanese: 「いや、フツーに普通の鳴がいいし」
lines.english: “Normal Naru is fine.”

lines.japanese: 「やーん言うと思ったーでも嬉しー、くねくねーくねくねー」
lines.english: “Eee, I knew you'd say that—but I'm so happy! Wriggle, wriggle, wriggle.”

lines.japanese: 「くねるな。肩をぶつけながらくねるな」
lines.english: “Stop wriggling. And stop ramming your shoulder into me while you do it.”

lines.japanese: 「へー意外。隼人先輩って、けっこー人前でイチャこくタイプだったんスね」
lines.english: “Huh. Never would've guessed you were the type to flirt in public, Hayato.”

lines.japanese: 「やーそうなんですよ実はこのひとめっちゃ甘えんぼさんでー！」
lines.english: “Oh, he is! The truth is, he's the clingiest little baby in the whole world!”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえよ、イチャこいてねえよ」
lines.english: “Shut up. We're not flirting.”

lines.japanese: 「強がり強がりー」
lines.english: “Putting on a tough act, putting on a tough act.”

lines.japanese: 「うぜえっつの。離れろ馬鹿、またイチャこいてるとか思われンだろ。俺のキャラってもんが──」
lines.english: “You're so damn annoying. Get off me, idiot. People are gonna think we're flirting again. I've got an image to maintain—”

lines.japanese: 「あ翔さん、おざまーす！」
lines.english: “Oh, morning, Kakeru!”
“—shit!”

lines.japanese: 「ぬゎーんちって！　うっそん、うっそォ～ん♪」
lines.english: “Psych! Gotcha, gotcha!”

lines.japanese: 「かかか、あんたら超ウケるわ。ちびっと皇帝の名前出しただけで、速攻１０メーターぐれー離れてやんの。しょーもねえ、どんだけビビって──」
lines.english: “Hahaha, you two are a riot. I only had to say the Emperor’s name and you shot ten meters apart. Seriously, how scared are you—”

lines.japanese: 「おい」
lines.english: “Hey.”
“—huh?”

lines.japanese: 「何がおかしいんだ？」
lines.english: “What's so funny?”

lines.japanese: 「笑ってンじゃねえよ、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Quit laughing, or I'll fucking kill you.”

lines.japanese: 「ひ、ひいいっ、ごめんなさい……！」
lines.english: “Eek! I'm sorry...!”

lines.japanese: 「てめ、どこ中だコラ。やんのか？　あ、やんのか？」
lines.english: “What middle school did you go to, asshole? You wanna go? Huh? You wanna fucking go?”

lines.japanese: 「よし、あとは任せる。適当に沈めとけ」
lines.english: “Great, I'll leave the rest to you. Sink him however you like.”

lines.japanese: さて、そろそろ時間だ。深夜バイトが始まる。オチは若い世代に委ねるとしよう。
lines.english: Well, it was about time. My late-night shift was starting. I'd leave the punch line to the younger generation.

lines.japanese: 去り際の目潰しピース。未来のメンマ組を頼んだぜ、後輩たち。
lines.english: One last eye-gouging peace sign as I left. The future of Menma's crew was in your hands, kids.

lines.japanese: 「ひぎぃ！」
lines.english: “Eeeeee!”

lines.japanese: 返事は絶叫だった。
lines.english: His answer was a scream.
